name: Fourth Political Theory
summary: Aleksandr Dugin's Fourth Political Theory proposes a new ideology to supersede liberalism, Marxism and fascism, taking existence itself (Dasein) rather than the individual, class or nation as the subject of politics. It is radically anti-liberal and anti-individualist, defends tradition, religion and the family, and calls for a multipolar world of sovereign civilization-states against Western hegemony. Dugin states it only as a set of parameters, so many practical policy questions are left open.
scope: Dugin's own Fourth Political Theory (2009 book, Arktos English edition 2012) as developed in his later writing and interviews, including his neo-Eurasianist geopolitics and Eurasia Party outlook. Positions are taken from his own recent articles and interviews on 4pt.su and the Wikipedia account of the book. It excludes other thinkers' revisions (such as Western personalist rewrites) and the broader Third Position and Eurasianist families.

sources.usedFor: Democracy, parliament, majority and minorities, separation of powers, legitimacy.

universal-healthcare.rationale: Dugin's social-justice, anti-liberal framing points to state-guaranteed basic services, but no source here speaks to healthcare itself.

raise-minimum-wage.rationale: Drawing on socialism's justice ideal without its materialism suggests support for state-set pay floors, though wages are never discussed.

markets-allocate-better.rationale: The theory rejects liberalism's primacy of the market and wants economic life subordinated to civilizational and state aims.

public-ownership.rationale: A strong sovereign state steering the economy fits public control of strategic utilities, but Dugin gives no specific program in these sources.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: Social justice and hostility to globalist liberal elites suggest higher taxes on the rich, but no tax position is stated.

unions-good.rationale: Dugin's corporatist, state-centred outlook makes independent unions neither central nor rejected; the sources are silent.

property-fundamental.rationale: Property rights as an individual absolute belong to the liberal individualism the theory attacks; private property is subordinated to the community.

regulate-corporations.rationale: Anti-globalist, anti-commercialisation stance favours subordinating big business to the state and national interest.

cut-welfare.rationale: Rejecting liberal individualism and welcoming social justice points against cutting welfare, though welfare is not discussed.

worker-ownership.rationale: The theory draws on socialism's ideals but is not syndicalist; nothing here addresses collective workplace ownership.

surveillance-ok.rationale: A statist, order-first outlook tends to accept security surveillance, though Dugin is not documented on this point.

legalize-drugs.rationale: Dugin laments Western moral decay and defends traditional values, which implies opposing drug legalization, but drugs are not mentioned.

restrict-hate-speech.rationale: Dugin attacks liberal-globalist speech norms and 'dictatorship' of correctness, so he would resist Western-style hate-speech laws.

strong-leader.rationale: He favours centralized leadership and argues that rotation of leaders at the top is the cardinal flaw of Western democracy.

state-harmful.rationale: He praises a strong, centralized sovereign state and civilizational state-power; the stateless position is the opposite of his stated doctrine.

limit-guns.rationale: Gun control is outside the theory and an order-focused statist could go either way.

empower-police-military.rationale: He argues military strength deters war and wants a strong state with firm order, so more authority for police and army fits.

legalize-sex-work.rationale: Traditional-values rhetoric and condemnation of Western moral collapse imply opposition, though sex work is never named.

decide-locally.rationale: He prizes centralized sovereign power and civilizational states, not decentralization to local level.

rehabilitation.rationale: The sources give nothing on penal philosophy and an order-focused traditionalist could favour either.

traditional-family.rationale: Dugin states that Russia stands for traditional values and laments that the indigenous West stopped having children and attacks the 'gender dictatorship'.

same-sex-marriage.rationale: He cites marches against same-sex marriage with sympathy and condemns the West for destroying its traditional values.

abortion-legal.rationale: Pro-natal traditionalism and complaint about falling birth rates imply opposition, though abortion is not mentioned in the sources.

more-religion-public.rationale: He calls his struggle a sacred war for God and traditional values and says democracy is not sacred because the last truth is God.

correct-racial-injustice.rationale: Rejecting liberal identity politics suggests opposition to remedial programs, but race-conscious policy is not discussed.

gender-social-construct.rationale: He condemns gender 'propaganda' and sex-change promotion as Western postmodern error, which rejects the constructionist view.

preserve-national-culture.rationale: He says liberal globalism destroys national and religious identity and sovereignty, and he defends the West's own traditional values.

gradual-change.rationale: The theory is a radical conservative revolution against liberal modernity, not incremental reform within established institutions.

reduce-immigration.rationale: He says masses of migrants were brought in by elite policy, that no normal European needs them, and endorses remigration.

empower-international-orgs.rationale: He rejects Western universal institutions yet wants the UN converted into an institution of multipolarity, so he opposes more power for it as it is.

free-trade.rationale: He backs economic sovereignty against dollar imperialism and Western-dominated trade.

nation-first.rationale: He puts sovereignty of civilization-states first, though his unit is the civilization-state, not a narrow nation.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: He rejects Western universal human-rights claims as provincial and opposes Western intervention as hegemony.

open-borders.rationale: He endorses remigration and says migration is a deliberate elite policy that destroys European society.

limit-growth.rationale: Anti-commercialisation critique of liberal capitalism gives some sympathy, but growth limits are not discussed and he favours state economic power.

drastic-climate-action.rationale: Climate policy is not addressed and he distrusts Western globalist agendas while criticizing technological modernity.

tech-solves-problems.rationale: The theory aims to use modernity's tools against itself and criticizes technological progress as substitute for human bonds.

expand-nuclear.rationale: A strategic, power-oriented outlook favours nuclear energy and weapons, but energy policy is not discussed.

revolution-justified.rationale: He calls for a conservative revolution against the liberal order, though against modernity rather than as class revolution.

experts-over-public.rationale: He says 'not everyone can think' yet bases legitimacy on the whole people supporting the state's course; the sources do not settle this.

central-planning.rationale: State direction of the economy and market subordination fit his program, though he is not documented endorsing full planning.

socialized-markets.rationale: The sources do not discuss market socialism; he wants markets subordinate to the state rather than owned by workers.

land-value-tax.rationale: Single tax proposals are not part of the theory and nothing in the sources bears on them.

tax-inheritance.rationale: Inheritance taxation is not discussed; traditionalism and social justice pull in opposite directions.

basic-income.rationale: Basic income is not addressed and no source indicates a position.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: He supports economic sovereignty and autarky of large spaces against Western dependency.

state-directs-investment.rationale: He calls for the state to move beyond import substitution toward autarky and strong economic sovereignty.

widespread-small-property.rationale: Distributist ownership is not discussed and the theory is not committed to it.

abolish-money-wages.rationale: He rejects Marxism for its materialism and linear progress, so abolishing money and wages is outside his theory.

abolish-central-banks.rationale: He attacks dollar imperialism but proposes no stance on central banking in these sources.

corporatist-bargaining.rationale: Third-position corporatism fits his statism, but organized bargaining bodies are not described.

one-party-rule.rationale: He wants support for the president's course across parties and criticizes party debate, yet no single guiding party is stated.

monarchy-legitimate.rationale: He prizes traditional organic forms of rule but no source states a monarchist position.

democracy-best.rationale: He says democracy is not sacred, calls Western liberal democracy a sham and rotation of leaders its cardinal flaw.

direct-votes.rationale: He favours a zemstvo democracy with the whole people behind the state's course and a Duma that assists authorities, not direct legislation.

workers-councils.rationale: He rejects class-centered Marxism as failed, and parliaments are replaced by state authority not councils.

right-to-secede.rationale: He wants centralized sovereignty and opposes separatism, though he backs breaking up the UK as decolonization.

natural-rulers.rationale: He says not everyone can think and sends intelligent people to legislate, implying unequal fitness to rule.

political-violence-never.rationale: He frames his struggle as a sacred war for God and traditional values and supports war against the West.

war-builds-character.rationale: He sees war as civilizational and metaphysical but says strength deters war, so character-building is not stated.

separate-church-state.rationale: He rejects Western secular separation, anchoring politics in the Logos and traditional faith, though not a theocracy.

laws-from-scripture.rationale: He wants religion and tradition to inform rule, yet scripture-based law is not stated as his program.

private-courts-defense.rationale: Privatizing the state's core functions contradicts his strong-state outlook and rejection of liberalism.

military-superiority.rationale: He argues that strength is the guarantee against world war and urges military alliances and readiness.

ethnic-nation.rationale: He builds on ethnos but rejects racial superiority and wants Eurasian multi-ethnic empire and federalism.

class-struggle-history.rationale: Dugin faults communism for focusing on class and linear progress; Dasein, not class, is the subject of politics.

equal-outcomes.rationale: He does not address equality and his logic is hierarchical, though he affirms social justice.

indigenous-land-authority.rationale: Indigenous land rights are not addressed in the sources.

colonial-reparations.rationale: He opposes Western hegemony and speaks of decolonization but reparations are not mentioned.

civilizational-union.rationale: He envisions civilization-states as poles of a multipolar world and Eurasian alliance of related civilizations.

self-interest-moral.rationale: Dugin condemns individualism and liberal self-interest, placing existence and tradition above the individual.

duties-before-rights.rationale: He calls individual rights and human-rights universalism Western and provincial and favours organically grown traditional forms.

nature-intrinsic-value.rationale: Ecology is not discussed; his traditionalism could value nature but sources say nothing.

limit-population.rationale: He laments that indigenous Europeans have too few children, so limits on population run against his position.

industrial-civilization-disaster.rationale: He attacks liberal modernity but affirms state power and technology as tools, so industrial civilization is not simply condemned.

accelerate-technology.rationale: He criticizes technology replacing human relationships and fears AI as challenge, so accelerating disruption is disfavoured.

human-enhancement.rationale: His defence of traditional values and complaint about sex-change propaganda point against technological redesign of the body.

algorithmic-government.rationale: He presents AI as civilizational challenge and values sacral human leadership, so ceding governance to algorithms is rejected.

unbreakable-encryption.rationale: A statist, order-first view would favour state access, though not documented.

restore-past-order.rationale: He rejects progress as racism against the past and wants return of tradition, but frames it as a new theory not restoration.

results-over-ideology.rationale: He is an ideological theorist who builds a new ideology; judging by results alone is not his approach.

direct-action.rationale: He works through state power and elections as support for the president, and he does not discuss direct action.

means-match-ends.rationale: Nothing in the sources addresses prefigurative method.

return-to-foraging.rationale: He affirms civilizations and states and uses modernity's tools, so a hunter-gatherer return is outside his view.

abolish-division-of-labor.rationale: It is a Marxist utopian aim that he rejects with Marxism's materialism.

distribute-by-need.rationale: He affirms social justice but not communism's distribution principle.

production-for-use.rationale: He opposes capitalism's fetishism of markets but this specific Marxian claim is not part of his stated program.

profit-exploitation.rationale: He rejects Marxism's class-based analysis, though he criticizes capitalism's commercialisation.

dictatorship-of-proletariat.rationale: Dugin states communism failed through its focus on class and its disregard for religion and he rejects class-centered politics.

collective-farming.rationale: Collectivized farming belongs to Marxist materialism he rejects but is not discussed directly.

capitalism-causes-war.rationale: He holds Atlanticist liberal hegemony drives conflict but not the Marxist thesis about capitalism.

taxation-theft.rationale: He rejects libertarian individualism; the strong sovereign state is central to his doctrine.

harm-principle.rationale: He criticizes liberal freedoms as dissolution and defends restricting 'gender propaganda' and traditional norms, rejecting a harm-only limit.

individual-rights-only.rationale: His theory replaces the individual with Dasein and traditional peoples as subject of politics and rejects individualism.

conscription.rationale: He urges strong military readiness and alliance, consistent with a state's power to conscript.

exit-over-voice.rationale: Exit as the key check on government is a libertarian view that contradicts his emphasis on sovereign unity.

state-as-business.rationale: He rejects liberal market logic and treats the state as sovereign and sacred in civilization terms, not a firm with customers.

positive-liberty.rationale: He criticizes liberal negative freedom but never speaks of material means for freedom.

media-academia-power.rationale: He says globalist elites are ruptured from society and spread ideology like a brain virus through liberal institutions.

hereditarian-race.rationale: Dugin says his theory strips out racism; he rejects racial superiority as a basis, though he does not discuss genetic ability.

organic-representation.rationale: He wants a zemstvo democracy and deputies advising the authorities, which suggests representation by communities rather than adversarial parties.

total-state.rationale: Sources record totalitarian-leaning remarks by critics, but his theory rejects state worship as fascism's flaw.

national-rebirth.rationale: He frames the West as decadent and his theory as renewal, though the nation is not his subject.

territorial-expansion.rationale: He calls for Russia to expand influence through alliances and conquest to build a Eurasian empire.

personal-loyalty-rule.rationale: Feudal personal oaths are not discussed and nothing suggests he advocates them.

bound-labor.rationale: Serfdom is not part of the theory and he draws on socialist social justice ideals.

no-neutral-knowledge.rationale: He holds that liberalism's universals are one civilization's view, so knowledge reflects culture and power in his account.

universal-morality.rationale: He says Western liberal universalism has proved deeply provincial and argues each civilization has its own values.

single-common-good.rationale: He wants unity behind the state's course rather than competing group interests, but a reasoned common good is not his phrase.

jewish-state-israel.rationale: Israel is not discussed in these sources.

diaspora-return-right.rationale: Diaspora return rights are not addressed in these sources.

workplace-democracy.rationale: Industrial democracy is a socialist form that he does not claim; his model is state-led.

school-vouchers.rationale: Market choice in schooling suits liberalism; he wants education as sacred civilizational formation.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: Fiscal policy is not addressed in the sources.

economic-freedom.rationale: He rejects liberalism's primacy of markets and the link between market freedom and political freedom.

rule-by-example.rationale: He values organic traditional forms of rule and sacral leadership, though example over law is not his phrase.

national-self-determination.rationale: He supports sovereignty of civilization-states, with the civilization as the unit, and opposes the West deciding for others.

force-without-un.rationale: He argues the UN must become a multipolar body and favours strength and independence from Western-led legality.

reason-over-faith.rationale: He says the source of mind is the Logos and criticizes modernity's excess of individualism and reason.

welfare-for-citizens.rationale: His hostility to mass migration suggests reserving benefits to natives, though welfare is not named.

class-collaboration.rationale: He rejects class struggle in favour of unity, and his third way blends capitalism and socialism.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: He condemns liberal contempt for the past as moral genocide against the past and defends tradition.

dominated-front.rationale: He calls on non-Western states to unite in a multipolar front against Western hegemony and cites BRICS measures against dollar imperialism.

workers-nation.rationale: He rejects class internationalism for community, ethnos and nation as the basis of solidarity.

distinct-gender-roles.rationale: He defends traditional family and attacks the 'gender dictatorship', implying distinct public roles.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: He distances the theory from fascism's racism and aims to remove racial supremacy.

state-class-instrument.rationale: He rejects class analysis and treats the state as sovereign and sacral rather than a class tool.

expand-fossil-fuels.rationale: Resource sovereignty and autarky favours domestic energy, though energy is not discussed.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: He endorses remigration and says migrants are unwanted; assimilation is a milder version of the same orientation.

elite-replacement.rationale: He says migrants were brought in by a conscious basic policy of European elites and that elites ruptured from society.

proportional-representation.rationale: He wants a Duma that assists authorities and no party debate, so electoral formulas are not at issue.

national-mission.rationale: He says Eurasian and Russian civilization has its own mission, though he opposes exporting a universal political form.

patriarchy-structural.rationale: He rejects gender ideology and defends traditional family roles, so he denies systematic male advantage as a framework.

political-elite-corrupt.rationale: He says globalist elites have completely ruptured with society and calls their ideology a brain virus.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Eugenics is a fascist element he removes; dysgenic language appears but no policy is stated.

security-forces-accountable.rationale: A statist emphasis on strong security forces suggests opposition to prosecuting past actions, but this is not discussed.

night-watchman-state.rationale: He advocates a centralized sovereign state with traditional values and rejects the liberal minimal state.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: He disclaims racism but defends ethnos and tradition; discouraging mixing is not a stated aim.

equal-moral-worth.rationale: His logic treats some groups as normal and others as pathological, and he rejects liberal universal equality.

socialism-one-country.rationale: He rejects Marxism and national Eurasian bloc-building, so world revolution is not required.

settler-state-colonial.rationale: Settler colonialism as a category is not addressed.

uniform-civil-code.rationale: Uniform civil code is not discussed; he allows religious traditions to shape societies.

restrict-conversion.rationale: Conversion law is not discussed in these sources.

ban-cattle-slaughter.rationale: He admires Hindutva but cattle slaughter is not mentioned.

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Eurasia Party-style thinking wants religion influential in education and culture, so he opposes a secular school mandate.

state-strengthens-encirclement.rationale: Socialist statecraft is not his doctrine; the question presupposes Marxism.

consent-of-governed.rationale: He roots authority in the state's course and God, not consent, and says democracy is not sacred.

trade-surplus.rationale: His economic sovereignty and autarky orientation fits mercantilist aims, but export balance is not discussed.

population-transfer.rationale: He endorses remigration, sending illegal or norm-violating residents back to their historical homeland.

initiating-force-wrong.rationale: He views a sacred war and military strength as legitimate, rejecting pacifist or libertarian non-aggression principle.

competition-drives-progress.rationale: He rejects linear progress, calling it racism against the past, and rejects the social Darwinist view of progress.

ban-extremist-parties.rationale: He notes sovereigntist parties face bans and objects, but he favours strong state power over challengers to civilizational order.

freedom-as-non-domination.rationale: Republican freedom theory is not addressed.

separated-powers.rationale: He says that Western liberal theory that separation and checking of powers is always better is a premise he rejects.

vanguard-party.rationale: He rejects Marxist class politics and the classical communist method.

priority-to-poor.rationale: He affirms social justice as a one-world brotherhood and a hybrid of socialist ideals with religion.

right-to-buy-council-homes.rationale: Mass privatization is liberal and not his program; housing is not discussed.

population-causes-poverty.rationale: He says indigenous Europeans no longer having children is the problem, not overpopulation.

diversity-weakens-cohesion.rationale: He argues mass migration produces chaos and that ethnos is the community basis of politics.

offices-by-lottery.rationale: He rejects Western procedural democracy and says intelligent people should be sent to legislate.

emergency-suspend-protections.rationale: He says Europe faces chaos or harsh dictatorship and defends order over liberal protections.

price-controls-essentials.rationale: State economic control fits his statism, but no source mentions price fixing.

party-controls-media.rationale: He wants patriotic media and ideological control, though Dugin's articles are not explicit on party control.

party-commands-army.rationale: His statist focus lies on sovereign state and its leader, not a party commanding the army.

long-naturalization-wait.rationale: He is hostile to mass immigration and wants unwanted migrants returned, implying restrictive citizenship.

party-discipline-binding.rationale: He says parties stand behind the president's course but party rules are not discussed.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: He opposes the destruction of sovereignty by liberal globalism, though he supports a Eurasian union of civilization poles.

head-commands-forces.rationale: He supports centralized leadership and a Duma that only assists authorities, matching executive control.

church-by-bishops.rationale: Church governance is not discussed, though he values Orthodoxy.

clerical-rule.rationale: His doctrine seeks religion's influence and a strong state, not rule by senior scholars.

defeat-own-government-war.rationale: He backs his own state in war, calling it a sacred war of civilizations.

censor-art-for-virtue.rationale: His attacks on liberal postmodern culture and for traditional values imply moral limits on art.

unlimited-reelection.rationale: He says that rotation of leaders at the top is the cardinal flaw of Western democracy.

recall-officials.rationale: He opposes rotation of leaders and the Western procedural model, and recall subjects leaders to voters.

end-foreign-alliances.rationale: He urges military alliances and a BRICS military pact as guarantees against war.

abolish-rental-housing.rationale: Housing is not addressed and abolition of rent is not part of his theory.

people-in-arms.rationale: His statism favours professional state armed forces, not armed citizenry.

rural-life-healthier.rationale: Traditionalist and anti-modernist outlook leans to rural life, but he does not discuss it.

reunify-divided-nation.rationale: He calls for Russian expansion and reuniting Russian-speaking lands, citing war over Ukraine as a civilizational struggle.

educated-out-of-touch.rationale: He says globalist elites have ruptured with society and attacks postmodern thinkers.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: He says every civilization-state has its own view of world order, but he claims Western universalism is a dead end and the West is deteriorating.

death-penalty.rationale: Order-first traditionalism favours capital punishment, though he is not documented on it.

sex-ed-in-schools.rationale: He denounces gender propaganda and defends traditional values in education.

creationism-in-schools.rationale: Religion in education is welcomed but no source touches on evolution.

restrict-pornography.rationale: Defence of traditional values and condemnation of Western moral collapse imply restriction.

citizenship-by-descent.rationale: His ethnos-based community concept and anti-migration views favour descent over territorial birth.

minority-language-support.rationale: Eurasia Party federalism gives ethno-cultural groups political status, so minority languages get support.

encourage-eccentricity.rationale: He rejects liberal individualism and values tradition over individual self-fashioning.

sovereign-debt-cancellation.rationale: He opposes dollar imperialism and supports a multipolar economic order.

independence-needs-economic-change.rationale: He links sovereignty to economic independence and urges autarky and exit from dollar dominance.

restrict-freedoms-for-growth.rationale: He prefers strong state order but this specific tradeoff is not stated.

rich-countries-aid-poor.rationale: He sees aid and liberal universalism as Western instruments, but aid is not discussed.

independent-nuclear-deterrent.rationale: He wants every pole to have strength and says strong military alignment prevents world war.

direct-election-head-of-state.rationale: He treats election as a referendum of support for the president, but electoral method is not specified.

central-bank-independence.rationale: Opposition to dollar imperialism and liberal technocracy suggests rejecting independent central banks.

no-land-for-peace.rationale: He backs territorial claims and war to keep Russian-claimed territory.

property-serves-common-good.rationale: Subordinating property to community and state interests follows from rejecting liberal individualism.

soviet-state-capitalist.rationale: He identifies Russia's side with Stalin and the Soviet state and does not apply that critique.

collective-defense.rationale: He urges strong military treaties and a BRICS military alliance as guarantees against war.

subordinate-church-to-state.rationale: Eurasia Party holds the church should be state-controlled yet influential, but Dugin's own view is mixed and not detailed.

nonpartisan-head-of-state.rationale: He places the president above parties with all parties behind him, as the embodiment of the state's course.

force-to-prevent-secession.rationale: He opposes separatism and centralizes authority, though he backs breakup of the UK.

sacred-ruler.rationale: He calls political struggle sacred and wants traditional organic rule, but not divine descent of rulers.

character-from-environment.rationale: Nature versus nurture is not addressed.

sovereign-above-law.rationale: He rejects separation of powers and favours strong central authority, though legal limits on rulers are not discussed.

mixed-constitution.rationale: He rejects checks and balances as a Western liberal premise, which is the mixed-constitution logic.

leader-cult.rationale: He frames the president as embodiment of the state's course and the people behind him.

class-struggle-under-socialism.rationale: He rejects class as analytic subject and Marxist theory.

refugee-return.rationale: He supports sending migrants home but does not address conflict refugees' return.

co-ethnic-territorial-claim.rationale: He treats war over Ukraine as a civilizational struggle and values Russian ethnos and Eurasian space.

apostasy-punishable.rationale: He values religion publicly but legal punishment of apostasy is not part of his stated positions.

women-must-cover.rationale: Dress codes are not mentioned and Russian Orthodox-oriented traditionalism does not require it.

common-currency.rationale: He attacks dollar imperialism and has BRICS payment alternatives in mind, but common currency is not specifically addressed.

kin-peoples-union.rationale: He envisions civilization poles and a Eurasian union of related peoples.

national-cultural-autonomy.rationale: Eurasia Party federalism gives ethno-cultural groups political and cultural expression within the state.

material-conditions-drive-history.rationale: He rejects Marxism's materialism and says tradition and Dasein, not economics, are the basis of politics.

no-bailouts.rationale: A statist order is more likely to intervene to protect national firms, but bailouts are not discussed.

courts-bound-by-majority.rationale: He says Western democracy's minority protections twist democracy into rule of minorities and favours a majority-backed state course.

gender-parity-bodies.rationale: He rejects gender ideology as Western postmodern error.

economic-self-sufficiency.rationale: He calls for autarky of large spaces and moving beyond import substitution to economic sovereignty.

trade-labor-env-standards.rationale: International trade standards are not addressed.

moral-incentives.rationale: His third way and moral-religious emphasis could favour moral incentives, but no source states it.

abolish-hereditary-privilege.rationale: He values traditional organic forms of rule but never addresses titles.

history-own-civilization.rationale: He defends teaching sacred civilizational identity and stresses civilizational identity.

civilizing-tutelage.rationale: He rejects Western universalist claim to civilize others as provincial, and argues each civilization has its own values.

patriotic-education.rationale: He calls education a sacred formation of the soul and civilizational identity and wants patriotic media.

end-racial-preferences.rationale: He opposes liberal identity politics, though preferences are not discussed.

public-money-creation.rationale: Money creation is not addressed, though he opposes dollar imperialism.

capitalism-adapts.rationale: Capitalist crisis theory is not addressed.

former-empire-influence.rationale: He calls for Russia to rebuild influence in lands of the Soviet and imperial space and for a Eurasian empire.

delink-world-market.rationale: He calls for autarky of large spaces and reduction of dependence on the Western-dominated order.

labor-aristocracy.rationale: Marxist theory of imperialism is not his framework.

freedom-to-discriminate.rationale: Libertarian property absolutism contradicts his outlook; he also is not a classical liberal.

entrenched-bill-of-rights.rationale: He rejects Western liberal constitutionalism and says democracy is not sacred.

colonial-treaties-void.rationale: He speaks of decolonization of Britain but treaties are not discussed.

elective-rulers.rationale: Legitimacy rests on the state's course and God, not on electing rulers, and he rejects rotation.

minority-veto.rationale: He rejects minority-rule democracy and defends a normal majority against minorities.

resist-lawless-ruler.rationale: He values strong central authority and does not endorse resistance to the ruler.

parliament-supreme.rationale: He says parliament is not a place for discussion and only assists the authorities.

noblesse-oblige.rationale: His social-justice emphasis and tradition suggest duties of the privileged, but not explicit.

withdraw-from-politics.rationale: He frames politics as a sacred war and urges active engagement.

mass-culture-pacifies.rationale: He criticizes technology, shopping malls and streaming as substitutes for real relationships.

ruling-class-consent.rationale: Gramscian hegemony is not part of his stated analysis.

world-economy-extracts-surplus.rationale: He opposes dollar imperialism and sees Western hegemony as extracting from other poles.

native-born-offices.rationale: His anti-migration and ethnos emphasis suggest it, though not stated.

party-own-road.rationale: Communist party relations are not his concern.

self-reliance-over-aid.rationale: He urges autarky and sovereignty against Western dependencies.

return-lost-territory.rationale: He supports Russian claims to Crimea and Donbas and Eurasian territorial recovery.

antifascism-founding-value.rationale: He seeks to supersede fascism with a new theory but does not treat anti-fascism as foundation.

totalitarianisms-equivalent.rationale: He draws on elements of fascism and communism and rejects the Western liberal equivalence.

slavery-not-civil-war-cause.rationale: American history debates are not addressed.

preserve-contested-monuments.rationale: He condemns liberal contempt for the past as moral genocide against the past.

male-disadvantage-attention.rationale: His critique of gender ideology implies sympathy, though men's disadvantage is not discussed.

institutions-fit-civilization.rationale: He says each civilization-state puts forward its own view of world order and that Western liberal democracy is not universal.

military-guardian-role.rationale: Strong armed forces are valued, but a political guardian role is not specified.

paid-care-work.rationale: Feminist care economics is not addressed.

filial-duty.rationale: His traditional family stance implies filial respect, though not stated explicitly.

office-by-exam.rationale: Civil service selection is not addressed, though his selection of capable legislators is vaguely related.

no-fault-divorce.rationale: Defence of traditional family implies opposition to easy divorce, though divorce is not discussed.

recallable-delegates.rationale: He says rotation of leaders is a flaw and the Duma helps authorities, rejecting delegate mandates.

individual-pension-accounts.rationale: Individualized private provision contradicts his anti-liberal outlook, but pensions are not discussed.

budget-needs-parliament.rationale: He says parliament assists authorities and rejects liberal checks, but the budget power is not discussed.

single-official-language.rationale: Strong state unity favours a common language, but his federalism allows ethnic expression.

foreign-land-ownership.rationale: Sovereignty and autarky favour barring foreign landholding.

disparate-impact-discrimination.rationale: He rejects liberal identity politics and minority-rule democracy.

consumerism-harmful.rationale: Dugin attacks capitalism's fetishism, commercialisation and shopping malls as replacing human bonds.

arm-foreign-insurgents.rationale: He treats the conflict with the West as total, but insurgent funding is not discussed.

intervene-in-bloc.rationale: He supports a Russian sphere and war in Ukraine as civilizational, but intervention in allies is not addressed.

corporate-influence.rationale: He blames globalist elites and capitalism's commercialisation for societal rupture.

restrict-foreign-funding.rationale: His sovereignty emphasis and fight against Western influence favour limiting foreign funding.

pronatalist-incentives.rationale: He laments that the indigenous population no longer has children and opposes migration as the answer.

residents-only-property.rationale: Local housing policy is not addressed.

job-guarantee.rationale: Social justice and statism incline toward job guarantees, but no position is stated.

democratic-peace.rationale: He regards democracy promotion as Western hegemony and liberal democracy as a dead end.

no-duty-to-obey.rationale: He advocates unity behind the sovereign state and its course as sacred.

non-intervention.rationale: He opposes Western intervention but defends Russian action in Ukraine, so absolute non-intervention is not his stance.

minority-conspiracy.rationale: He says elites conspire in migration policy, but no ethnic or religious minority is named.

abolish-legal-marriage.rationale: He champions traditional family and rejects same-sex marriage, so abolishing legal marriage opposes him.

public-access-to-information.rationale: He wants patriotic media and a state-directed course; transparency rights are not discussed.

local-production.rationale: His autarky emphasis implies preference for domestic production, though not local scale.

informal-organisation.rationale: He supports a state-led order rather than loose anarchist groups.

national-law-over-international.rationale: He rejects Western-dominated international institutions and defends sovereignty.

religious-nation.rationale: He grounds civilization-states in religious and traditional foundations, such as Orthodoxy and Hindutva.

deference-to-leading-power.rationale: He supports multipolarity with each pole sovereign, not tribute.

regional-revenue-retention.rationale: Centralized authority is preferred; fiscal federalism is not discussed.

personal-possessions-private.rationale: Marxian property distinction is not discussed.

defeat-communism.rationale: He treats communism as failed but sees it as an element to integrate, and praises the Soviet past.

religion-illusion.rationale: He says the last truth is God and that the source of mind is the Logos, rejecting religion as illusion.

capitalism-progressive.rationale: He rejects linear progress and capitalism's fetishism, so he does not see capitalism as progressive.

women-equality-needs-economic-change.rationale: Feminist framing is rejected as gender ideology.

socialized-care.rationale: His traditional family stance rejects socializing family functions.

treaties-binding.rationale: Treaties with internal nations are not discussed.

cooperative-communities.rationale: Small communes are not part of his state-centred theory.

majority-settlement.rationale: He prioritizes Russians as ethnos in federalism but settlement policy is not discussed.

neither-capitalism-nor-communism.rationale: Dugin presents the theory as neither fascism, nor communism, nor liberalism and draws on a third-way tradition.

historical-land-claim.rationale: He grounds claims on civilizational and historical space and backs Crimea's annexation.

holocaust-denial.rationale: He calls Nazism and its racial supremacy a flaw; Holocaust denial is not part of the theory.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: He is hostile to LGBT rights, but criminal penalties are not stated in the sources.

suppress-opposition.rationale: He warns of dictatorship and praises order, but suppression is not explicitly urged.

punish-blasphemy.rationale: He frames politics as a sacred war for God, but blasphemy law is not discussed.

colonies-serve-metropole.rationale: He supports decolonization and opposes Western imperial hegemony.

defensive-jihad-duty.rationale: Islamic jurisprudence is not his; he treats Islamic civilization as a pole.

unreligious-rulers-fought.rationale: He values religion in politics but does not endorse removing secular rulers.

participatory-democracy.rationale: He favours centralized leadership and a Duma that assists authorities, not mass participation.

intersecting-oppressions.rationale: He rejects identity politics as a postmodern error that isolates people.

gender-identity-recognition.rationale: He condemns pushing sex change through propaganda and the gender dictatorship.

assisted-dying.rationale: Traditional religious values suggest opposition, though not discussed.

left-right-obsolete.rationale: Dugin's theory is described as beyond left and right but against the centre, integrating elements of all three theories.

alienated-labor.rationale: He criticizes capitalism's commercialisation, but the Marxist concept is not his.

islam-incompatible.rationale: He treats Islam as a legitimate civilization and religion and wants alliances with Muslim states.

divine-source-of-authority.rationale: He says democracy is not sacred and the last truth is God and ties politics to the Logos and sacred war.

religious-dress-in-state.rationale: Public religion is welcomed, but dress is not discussed.

social-market-economy.rationale: He mixes capitalism and socialism but via state command, not a social market model.

abolish-armed-forces.rationale: He insists strength deters war and urges military treaties.

stay-neutral-between-blocs.rationale: He wants Russia aligned in a Eurasian bloc against the West, not neutral.

dynastic-succession.rationale: He opposes rotation of leaders but dynastic transmission is not discussed.

refuse-lender-austerity.rationale: He rejects dollar imperialism and Western financial hegemony.

property-franchise.rationale: Franchise is not discussed; he rejects liberal democracy but defends whole-people support.

domination-women-nature.rationale: Eco-feminist claims fit the gender ideology he rejects.

reification.rationale: Marxist critique is not his framework, though he criticizes commercialisation.

press-owned-by-wealth.rationale: He says elites have captured institutions, but the Marxist framing of press freedom is not his.

racial-franchise.rationale: He says his theory strips out racism and rejects racial hierarchy.

online-participation.rationale: Mass deliberation conflicts with his state-led model.

open-government-data.rationale: Transparency is not discussed and a state-led model prefers control.

boycott-minority-shops.rationale: He is not documented endorsing boycotts of religious minorities.

citizens-assembly.rationale: Deliberative mini-publics conflict with unity behind the state course.

reinterpret-religion.rationale: He treats traditions as organically grown foundations to be defended, not reformed.

wealth-concentration-endangers-liberty.rationale: Liberty is not his central frame, though he is hostile to capitalist elites.

open-lgbt-military-service.rationale: He opposes LGBT policy as Western propaganda and defends traditional values.

state-promotes-atheism.rationale: He faults communism for disregarding religion and says the last truth is God.

abolish-police-prisons.rationale: He wants strong state authority and order.

power-sharing-divided-societies.rationale: Consociationalism is not discussed, though Eurasia Party federalism gives ethnic groups status.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: His social-justice emphasis favours state responsibility over private charity.

term-limits.rationale: He calls rotation of leaders at the top the cardinal flaw of Western democracy.

vote-delegation.rationale: Liquid democracy conflicts with his view of parliament as assisting the authorities.

existential-risk-priority.rationale: Transhumanist risk is not discussed, though AI is treated as civilizational challenge.

women-in-religious-leadership.rationale: His traditionalism suggests opposition, but religious office is not discussed.

foreign-residents-local-vote.rationale: His hostility to mass migration and emphasis on sovereignty oppose it.

uniformed-youth.rationale: His emphasis on civilizational education and strong state suits it, but not documented.

no-nuclear-weapons-on-territory.rationale: Basing is not discussed, though nuclear power is valued as strength.

no-foreign-bases.rationale: He opposes Atlanticist control and US strategic presence.

income-for-work-not-ownership.rationale: Anti-commercialisation and social justice incline this way, but not stated.

never-kill-self-defence.rationale: He argues strength and war are necessary and sacred in defence.

unbroken-national-continuity.rationale: He roots civilization-states in organically grown traditional foundations.

sex-socially-constructed.rationale: He rejects gender ideology as propaganda.

no-fixed-category-of-women.rationale: He rejects postmodern identity politics and gender ideology.

martyrs-honoured.rationale: He frames the war as sacred for God and traditional values, which implies honouring the fallen.

politics-spiritual-struggle.rationale: He describes his political struggle as a sacred war for God and traditional values and the war as metaphysical.

homeland-cultural-centre.rationale: Diaspora homeland theory is not discussed.

culture-before-state.rationale: He emphasizes the sovereign state and civilizational power as central.

god-not-male.rationale: Orthodox-based traditionalism favours traditional language, but it is not discussed.

scripture-judged-by-women.rationale: He rejects feminist and postmodern critique of tradition.

economy-in-majority-hands.rationale: National-priority economics fits, but not documented.

single-unit-for-people.rationale: Russian ethnos as priority and Eurasian unity are consistent, but administrative merging is not discussed.

independent-unions.rationale: Statism and corporatism favour union subordination to the state, but unions are not discussed.

socialism-needs-workers-power.rationale: He rejects class-based Marxism as failed.

municipal-property.rationale: Municipal socialism is not his model.

confederal-coordination.rationale: He favours centralized sovereignty, not libertarian municipalism.

family-wage.rationale: His traditional family stance and social justice suggest family-supporting wages.

faster-drug-approval.rationale: Regulation of drugs is not discussed.

ageing-research-funding.rationale: Transhumanist projects conflict with his traditionalism.

anonymous-payments.rationale: State control orientation opposes untraceable payments, but not documented.

online-anonymity.rationale: He favours state order and information control, but it is not documented.

person-over-state.rationale: He replaces the individual with Dasein as the subject and subordinates the individual to community and civilization.

spiritual-nature.rationale: He grounds politics in the Logos, tradition and the sacred, rejecting materialism.

regional-powers-revocable.rationale: He prefers centralized sovereignty over regional autonomy.

racial-group-interests.rationale: He disclaims race as the basis, preferring ethnos, civilization and religion.

racial-pride.rationale: Race is not his category, so pride in it is neither affirmed nor rejected.

defensive-wars-only.rationale: He supports war in Ukraine as civilizational, expansion of influence and conquest.

language-defines-nation.rationale: His ethnos includes shared language, but he holds civilizations unite across languages.

foreign-partition-plot.rationale: He claims the West plots to weaken Russia and fragment it, and suggests breaking up the UK as counterplay.

future-generations.rationale: Tradition and continuity support obligations to future generations, but it is not discussed.

women-distinct-values.rationale: Traditional gender views imply distinct feminine values, but not stated.

arms-reduction.rationale: He says strength deters war and military alliances are the guarantee.

capital-controls.rationale: Economic sovereignty and autarky favour capital controls.

state-arms-monopoly.rationale: His strong state favours monopoly of force.

soldiers-refuse-war.rationale: He views war as sacred and urges strength.

in-work-tax-credits.rationale: Tax credit design is not discussed.

restructure-world-economy.rationale: He calls for ending dollar imperialism and a multipolar economic order.

smash-state-machine.rationale: He advocates a strong centralized state, not smashing it.

free-economic-experiment.rationale: He favours a state-guided economy and a third way over open experimentation.

nature-as-capital.rationale: Capitalizing nature is a liberal-market approach he opposes.

sacred-nation.rationale: He treats community, ethnos and civilization as sacred, though the nation is not his subject; the state-civilization is.

shared-human-nature.rationale: He rejects a universal human nature behind rights and says civilizations have their own values.

public-service-media.rationale: Media funding is not discussed; he wants patriotic media.

religions-one-truth.rationale: Traditionalism of the Guenon type holds a primordial unity of traditions.

farm-price-support.rationale: State economic protection of producers fits, but not discussed.

keep-nuclear-weapons.rationale: He argues strength and military capacity deter world war.

workers-own-party.rationale: He rejects class-based politics and party debate.

women-property-inheritance.rationale: Property rights of women are not discussed.

pollution-tort-liability.rationale: Tort-based environmental law is not discussed.

customary-chiefs-lawmaking.rationale: Customary chiefs are not discussed, though traditional forms of rule are praised.

mandatory-sentences.rationale: Order-first outlook suggests fixed sentences, but not discussed.

immigrants-learn-language.rationale: His restrictionist stance suggests language requirements.

religious-equal-recognition.rationale: He treats multiple religions as legitimate civilization pillars, but state recognition is not addressed.

democracy-is-procedure.rationale: He says democracy is not sacred, calls Western democracy a sham and reframes elections as support for the state's course.

premarital-sex.rationale: Traditional values imply disapproval, but it is not stated.

internet-shutdowns.rationale: Order-first statism favours it, but not discussed.

women-suffrage.rationale: Suffrage is not discussed and he is skeptical of democracy.

religion-oppresses-women.rationale: He defends religion and the traditional family and rejects feminist critique.

homestead-ownership.rationale: Lockean appropriation is a libertarian individualist view.

international-criminal-courts.rationale: He rejects Western-led universal institutions and defends sovereignty.

scripture-inerrant.rationale: Orthodox traditionalism values scripture but literalism is not stated.

gendered-self-government.rationale: Gender guarantees conflict with his stance on gender ideology.

defend-planned-state.rationale: Trotskyist defense is not his framework.

indirect-election.rationale: He prefers state-guided selection, but indirect election is not stated.

national-church-status.rationale: He wants the church influential in society, though Eurasia Party also supports other traditional religions.

minority-territorial-autonomy.rationale: Eurasia Party federalism gives ethno-cultural groups the status of political subjects.

disputed-territory-plebiscite.rationale: He claims territory by civilization and history, but his position on plebiscites is not stated.

keep-colonial-borders.rationale: He seeks Russian influence in imperial space and rejects colonial arrangements.

homeland-spiritual-bond.rationale: He treats land and civilization as sacred spaces.

extrajudicial-killing.rationale: Not documented, and he is not a Duterte-style advocate.

close-ties-china.rationale: He cites Russia and China as civilization poles allied against Western hegemony.

protect-kin-minorities.rationale: He backs war to protect Russian speakers in Ukraine as civilizational duty.

resources-common-ownership.rationale: Georgist claims are not part of his framework.

self-ownership.rationale: Libertarian self-ownership contradicts his rejection of individualism.

targeted-social-spending.rationale: He values social justice but not means-testing, and not discussed.

bypass-parties-groups.rationale: He says parliament assists authorities and the whole people stands behind the president directly.

no-business-privileges.rationale: He opposes oligarchic clans, but not discussed in sources.

no-denominational-politics.rationale: Not discussed; he treats religion as civilizational.

tech-with-ancestral-values.rationale: He aims to use modernity's tools against itself and combine them with traditional worldview.

wife-divorce-without-consent.rationale: Traditional family implies disfavour, but not stated.

national-resource-control.rationale: He supports economic sovereignty and autarky and defies dollar imperialism.

constituent-assembly.rationale: He treats Russia's 1990s liberal constitution as partly absorbed Western theory and favours a zemstvo-style democracy over procedural constitution-making.

annexed-territory-occupation.rationale: He backed the 2014 annexation of Crimea and frames the war as civilizational, so he rejects calling annexed territory occupied.

foreign-takeover-block.rationale: His call for economic sovereignty and autarky against Western dependency favours blocking foreign purchase of strategic firms.

multipolar-world.rationale: Dugin calls for a multipolar order of civilization-states, each with its own values.

distribution-by-process.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's critique of liberal individualism and capitalism as the subject-less order to be superseded; distribution is not discussed.

financial-transactions-tax.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's hostility to globalist finance and liberal elites; no source mentions such a tax.

racism-not-main-obstacle.rationale: Dugin rejects liberal anti-racism discourse yet also rejects biological racism in favour of ethnos, so the statement does not map cleanly.

unjust-law-not-binding.rationale: Dugin's sources discuss legitimacy and democracy but not the natural-law question, so this is unclear.

automate-paid-work.rationale: Inferred from the theory's critique of progress and technological modernity.

labour-theory-of-value.rationale: Inferred from the theory's rejection of Marxist materialism as one of the three modern ideologies to be superseded.

patriotism-serves-workers.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's blend of social justice, tradition and sovereignty with Eurasian national loyalty, though he does not use this wording.

material-over-identity.rationale: Inferred: the theory takes Dasein and ethnos, not material class interest, as its political subject.

market-under-party-rule.rationale: Inferred from Dugin's rejection of Marxism and of both liberal markets and one-party communist rule.

missingStatements.text: Existence, tradition and community, not the individual, class or nation, should be the basic subject of politics.
missingStatements.rationale: The book's central claim is that Dasein, not the individual, class or nation, is the subject of politics.
missingStatements.declined: Abstract Heideggerian claim that few other ideologies could answer; neither-capitalism-nor-communism and culture-before-state cover it.

missingStatements.text: The world should be organised as several sovereign civilization-states rather than under one dominant power.
missingStatements.rationale: Dugin calls for a multipolar order of civilization-states, each with its own values.

missingStatements.text: Western liberal democracy and its human-rights norms are the product of one civilization and should not be imposed on others.
missingStatements.rationale: Dugin calls Western liberal universalism provincial and a dead end and says democracy is not sacred.

notes: Dugin gives the theory as parameters rather than a program, so economic and many social-policy answers are low-confidence inferences from his anti-liberal, traditionalist and statist writings. Critics describe parts of his outlook as far-right or fascist; Dugin himself says the theory removes racism and state worship. Quotations about migration and LGBT people in his articles are his assertions and are not verified claims.
